INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
  SUMMER INTERNSHIP
  
                    Harsh Gawli
                           TY B.Tech CS

Round 1: Online Assessment
Eligibility Criteria - CS, IT and EXTC students could apply with CGPA > 7.0
The online assessment consisted of 61 questions(1 coding question and 60 MCQs) 
which were to be solved in 80 mins. The assessment took place on HackerRank.
1.
The MCQs consisted of theory questions related to Java, OOPs in Java, SQL and 
aptitude questions(pattern-based questions).
2.
I don’t remember the exact coding question, but it was a variation of this question 
so do go through it. I was able to pass 13/15 test cases.
The test results were announced on 27 January and 8 students were shortlisted for the 
interview and I was one of them. We were informed that the interview will take place 
in offline mode in the UBS office at Airoli. We were given time slots for our 
interview and were asked to be present 10 - 15 mins prior to our time slot.
Interview Round (31 January):
In the email that we received, everyone was assigned 2 interviewers. For some, both 
the interviews were developers while for some one of the interviewers was the HR 
and one was an associate director, the latter being my case. My interview began at 
11:15am.
The interviewers were friendly and made sure that I was comfortable and not nervous 
throughout the interview. The associate director was a guy, and the HR was a woman.
The interview began with a discussion on my projects. I was asked to explain the 
very first project on my resume(what is the end goal of the project, the tech stack 
used in the project, why the particular tech stack was used, the code logic used for a 
specific functionality and so on). The interviewers didn’t seem very impressed at 
first. Then, one of the interviewers asked me which of the projects that I had 
mentioned was very close to my heart, to which I replied the very first full-stack 
website that I had developed and deployed. So I started explaining this project and 
this time they were content with my explanation. 
Next, I was asked some theory questions on DBMS - What is the difference between 
DELETE, DROP and TRUNCATE; What is a view and what are its advantages.

Next, the interviewer moved on to DSA and asked me what algorithms (searching 
and sorting) I was aware of. So I listed all the algorithms I was confident about. The 
interviewers didn’t ask me anything more on this topic.
My HR round began in this very slot itself. 
The very first question that I was asked was “Why do you want to join UBS”. I had 
an answer prepared for this. For this question, always the check the company website 
and jot down stuff like “Principles of ABC company” or “Our motto” etc. Next, I was 
asked if I knew the difference between retail banking and investment banking. I had a 
rough idea about the difference between the two so I answered this question and the 
interviewer also added some extra points and gave me a brief idea about the 
differences. 
Next, the HR asked me if I kept myself up to date with current affairs to which I 
replied not much as I was busy preparing for internships. She proceeded to ask me 
some questions on current affairs like what are your views on the Russia-Ukraine 
conflict.
Finally, the interviews asked me if I had any questions for them. Always ask 1-2 
questions as it shows that you’re interested. So I asked them how has their experience 
been working in UBS and whether interns get to work on new projects or on-going 
projects. The interviewers answered both questions. After this, my interview ended.
The interview lasted for about 40-45 mins.
Now, only one round was conducted for all the 8 students but for some, the interview 
was entirely technical.
On 8 February the results were announced. 6 students were selected for the 
internship and I was lucky to be one of those 6.

Some useful resources:
1.
DSA - Striver’s SDE sheet
2.
DBMS - Gate smashers playlist and last minute revision notes on GFG.
3.
OS - Gate Smashers playlist.
Be thoroughly prepared with your projects - the motivation behind the project, if 
developed during a hackathon then be ready with the problem statement that you 
aimed to solve using the website/app that you developed as group, the tech stack used 
in the project, why the tech was used, what are the alternatives, etc.
All the best!!
